pages.text: Odenkey had a round, red, itchy patch on his arm. He tried to hide it under his sleeve. He felt shy and worried. “What if the others laugh?” he thought. At last, he quietly told Madam Kumi.
sentences: Odenkey had a round, red, itchy patch on his arm.
He tried to hide it under his sleeve.
He felt shy and worried.
“What if the others laugh?” he thought.
At last, he quietly told Madam Kumi.
pages.alt: Beside the classroom desk, shy Odenkey holds his forearm near his shirt sleeve as he speaks quietly to kind, attentive Madam Kumi.

pages.text: Madam Kumi took him to Nurse Azumah. The nurse looked at the patch gently. “This is ringworm,” she said. “It is a skin infection caused by a tiny living thing called a fungus. It is not a worm, and it does not mean you are dirty. Many children get it.”
sentences: Madam Kumi took him to Nurse Azumah.
The nurse looked at the patch gently.
“This is ringworm,” she said.
“It is a skin infection caused by a tiny living thing called a fungus.
It is not a worm, and it does not mean you are dirty.
Many children get it.”
pages.alt: In a bright, welcoming school clinic room, smiling Nurse Azumah in a white coat gently looks at a small round mark on Odenkey’s forearm while Madam Kumi stands reassuringly nearby.

pages.text: “Ringworm spreads when we touch the patch, or when we share combs, towels, caps and clothes with someone who has it,” said Nurse Azumah. “So we keep our own personal items, keep our skin clean and dry, and wash our hands.”
sentences: “Ringworm spreads when we touch the patch, or when we share combs, towels, caps and clothes with someone who has it,” said Nurse Azumah.
“So we keep our own personal items, keep our skin clean and dry, and wash our hands.”
pages.alt: Nurse Azumah pointing to a wordless picture card showing a hair comb, a folded hand towel and a cap, explaining good hygiene habits to Odenkey.

pages.text: “I will give you medicine to put on the patch,” said the nurse. “Use it every day with a grown-up’s help, for as long as I say, even after the patch looks better. Try not to scratch it, and wash your hands after touching it.” Odenkey nodded.
sentences: “I will give you medicine to put on the patch,” said the nurse.
“Use it every day with a grown-up’s help, for as long as I say, even after the patch looks better.
Try not to scratch it, and wash your hands after touching it.” Odenkey nodded.
pages.alt: Nurse Azumah handing a small plain white ointment tube to Madam Kumi and smiling Odenkey beside a clean handwashing sink in the school clinic.

pages.text: The next day, Madam Kumi spoke kindly to the class. “Skin infections can happen to anyone. We never tease. We do not share combs, towels or caps, and we tell a grown-up whenever we notice a rash or an itchy patch.” Zakaria held up his comb. “I will always use my own comb,” he said.

pages.alt: In the sunny classroom, Madam Kumi speaks warmly to the pupils while smiling Zakaria holds up his own small comb from his school bag beside Odenkey.

pages.text: After a few weeks, the patch healed completely. Odenkey felt happy and confident again. “I am glad I told Madam Kumi,” he said. “It is always better to ask for help early.” His friends cheered as they ran out to play together.
sentences: After a few weeks, the patch healed completely.
Odenkey felt happy and confident again.
“I am glad I told Madam Kumi,” he said.
“It is always better to ask for help early.” His friends cheered as they ran out to play together.
pages.alt: In the bright schoolyard at break time, happy Odenkey with healthy clear arms laughs and runs out to play football with Zakaria and their classmates.
